findings.claim: The planning-only scope guard is fail-open and does not prevent pre-staged runtime files from entering the commit.
findings.analysis: The runtime-path check ends with `|| true`, so it succeeds even when runtime diffs exist. The later path-scoped `git add` does not remove files already staged before the sequence, while `git diff --cached --check` checks formatting rather than the allowed path set. T5 can therefore commit runtime changes while reporting planning-only success.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `|| true` and add a fail-closed staged-path allowlist immediately before commit that rejects every path outside `docs/specs/**`, `docs/plans/**`, and `proposals/**`.

findings.claim: Several authoritative artifacts still treat PR #10 as open and WI-547 as in progress despite both being landed.
findings.analysis: The manifest and index correctly record PR #10 and WI-547 as landed, and the merge-base is the required `223436ab`. However, the reconciliation base and unblock section, architecture rollback, solution-confidence current-state and action packet, feature dependency text, and WI-548 context still describe an open PR #10, an intact WI-547 worktree, or a future rebase. These contradictory instructions can cause re-closeout or obsolete rollback work.
findings.proposed_fix: Rebase every current-state, rollback, dependency, and closeout statement onto the landed reality: WI-547 is immutable VERIFIED-L3, PR #10 is merged, and neither has remaining execution in this DAG.

findings.claim: AC-548-5 is marked complete although WI-545 and WI-546 are not implementation-ready child specifications.
findings.analysis: AC-548-5 requires each independently landable child to have ACs, files, tests, rollback, and cost notes. WI-545 has broad scope and affected files but no enumerated ACs, deterministic test plan, rollback, or cost section. WI-546 has broad scope but no enumerated ACs, rollback, provider-cost section, or exact fixture commands. T2 validates only that listed items have rows, which cannot establish AC-548-5.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit AC, affected-file, focused-test, rollback, and provider-cost sections to WI-545 and WI-546, then make T2 validate those sections rather than row existence.

findings.claim: The child dependency DAG is contradictory and cannot be scheduled deterministically.
findings.analysis: WI-546 declares `Depends on: —` while its status and reconciliation require multiple predecessors. The reconciliation makes WI-552 conditional using the undefined phrase `if restart fixtures are in the wave`, yet the capability matrix requires restart continuation in the final acceptance wave. WI-551 is required to prevent hidden remapping and is a prerequisite of WI-552, but is omitted from WI-546's stated prerequisite set. WI-553 is shown parallel in one ordering without a clear landing-boundary relationship.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one canonical DAG with explicit hard and optional edges. State mechanically whether WI-546 depends on WI-551 and WI-552, define the condition controlling restart fixtures, and mirror those edges in every child header, the manifest, and reconciliation.

findings.claim: WI-550 does not require a concurrent-writer proof for its atomic receipt-merge claim.
findings.analysis: The architecture requires atomic sibling merging, but WI-550 tests only sequential writes and same-key overwrite rejection. Two processes writing distinct WI keys to the same notes envelope can still race through read-modify-write and lose one receipt while all listed sequential fixtures pass.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an AC defining the lock/CAS/retry primitive and a barrier-synchronized concurrent-writer fixture proving both distinct-WI receipts survive or one writer fails explicitly without data loss.

findings.claim: Several child rollback plans deliberately restore the false-success behavior the program is intended to eliminate.
findings.analysis: WI-550 rollback restores type-only keys and therefore known last-wins corruption. WI-551 rollback restores prior host tables even though the current path silently remaps unknown hosts, while prose merely says not to reintroduce that behavior. WI-549 removes the shared resolver without defining the replacement that preserves fail-closed missing-policy behavior. These are warnings, not executable safe rollback procedures.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify safety-preserving rollback states: disable new writes while retaining composite reads for WI-550, preserve explicit unknown-host refusal for WI-551, and retain a minimal common-dir fail-closed resolver for WI-549.

findings.claim: T4 is recorded as promoted even though its declared launcher-receipt checkpoint is absent and its mechanical evidence is disposable.
findings.analysis: The manifest requires a review log plus launcher receipt. The review log records a launcher exit and a `/tmp` mechanical log but no durable receipt path or digest binding the mechanical result, manifest tree, and review result. It then declares `PROMOTED_WITH_DISPUTES` while T5, the PR URL, and the owner gate remain incomplete. This creates a false terminal state even though the stated mechanical pass itself is accepted as factual.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind T4 to a durable review receipt containing the reviewed tree or manifest digest and mechanical result digest. Use a review-complete state rather than PROMOTED until T5 actually opens the planning PR.

findings.claim: The finalization barrier does not define which receipt set must validate at each implementation, promotion, closeout, Stop, and VERIFIED transition.
findings.analysis: The architecture names several SHA classes, while WI-550 reduces the rule to the exact closeout SHA. No matrix specifies required receipt types, WI identity, phase, target SHA, and consumer for each transition. An implementation can therefore validate a convenient valid SHA while omitting the receipts belonging to the actual transition.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a transition matrix mapping every completion consumer to its canonical SHA source, required receipt identities, allowed legacy projection, and fail-closed behavior.
